{{Quote|The ion cannon will fire several shots to make sure that any enemy ships will be out of your flight path.|[[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]|<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref>}}
The '''v-150 Planet Defender''' was a surface-to-[[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]] produced by [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]].

==Description==
[[File:V150PlanetDefender-InsideTheWorldsOfSWTrilogy.jpg|thumb|200px|left|Schematics of the v-150 Planet Defender on Hoth]]
Manufactured by [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]], the v-150 Planet Defender was a massive, independently powered, surface-based [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]] designed to target and neutralize [[Starship/Legends|starships]] in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] of a [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. The v-150 was usually mounted on a rotating base, and the weapon itself was covered by a semi-spherical shell of reinforced [[Permacite/Legends|permacite]]. The weapon was designed to be modular, with an installation time of only a few [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]].<ref name="ISB" />

Each weapon was sold with its own reactor, which was intended to be buried forty [[Meter/Legends|meters]] below the weapon emplacement. Three levels of crew quarters and storage space were located between the reactor and the weapon, and the emplacement could store enough supplies to last the crew of twenty-seven for three [[Standard month/Legends|months]].<ref name="ISB" /> When activated, it took several [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]] for the v-150 to maneuver into position on its rotating base.<ref name="EGWT">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> The v-150 was completely immobile, and was vulnerable to attack from ground forces and aerial bombardment. A retractable blast shield protected the weapon, and the cover had to be retracted to fire the weapon.<ref name="NEGWT" />

The v-150 took targeting data from [[Electrotelescope/Legends|electrotelescopes]] and long-range [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]], and could also be linked to orbital sensor stations for more accurate targeting. The weapon had an optimum range of 4,000 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]], and a maximum range of 180,000 kilometers.<ref name="NEGWT" /> The v-150's fire-control [[Computer/Legends|computers]] allowed the v-150 to target orbital ships at will, and a single ion bolt could disrupt [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers]].<ref name="ISB" /> The weapon had a fire rate of one shot every six [[Standard second|seconds]].<ref name="EGWT" />

The v-150 was commonly employed in conjunction with [[Planetary shield/Legends|planetary shields]]; as planetary shields were expensive to maintain, planets only powered them up when they were needed. Even then, the shields could take several minutes to reach full power. It was during these minutes that the v-150 was vital to planetary defense, targeting enemy vessels in orbit before the shield could reach full power.<ref name="ISB" />

The v-150 was expensive,<ref name="ISB" /> costing between 500,000<ref name="ISB2" /> and 1.5 million [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]],<ref name="RECG" /> which was a quarter of the price of a full planetary shield.<ref name="ISB" /> Planetary ion cannons were synchronized with planetary shields to allow the weapon to fire through the shields by lowering them for a split second. Even with the rotational base, each ion cannon had a limited fire vector of a few hundred square kilometers, so they were placed to protect vital bases, shield generators, [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]] and [[City/Legends|cities]].<ref name="EGWT" />

==History==
The v-150 Planet Defender was first proposed by a [[Gathi]] working for [[CoMar Combat Systems/Legends|CoMar Combat Systems]] named [[Can Lar]]. CoMar rejected his proposal, stating that the design was "militarily useless and an engineering impossibility." In response, Lar quit CoMar and attempted to find an employer that would take his design seriously. He found it in [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]].<ref name="ISB" />

Many Imperial planets bought v-150s to supplement their defense setup and to reduce the cost of keeping their planetary shields active.<ref name="ISB" /> The planetary ion cannons used by the Alliance were stolen during a hijack of a [[Super Transport series|super transport]] in the [[Kuat system/Legends|Kuat system]]. The ion cannons were assigned to [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], and [[Bulwark]]. The others were at highly classified locations.<ref name="GG3">''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref>

The [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] colony [[Kothlis/Legends|Kothlis]] was protected by a hidden V-150. Originally funded by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], in the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Era]] it was maintained by the local [[Imperial compound (Kothlis)|Imperial consulate]], supplemented by [[Beldonna's League|mercenaries]].<ref name="SOTE Planets Guide">''[[Shadows of the Empire Planets Guide]]''</ref>

[[File:Planet_Defender.png|thumb|200px|right|A v-150 Planet Defender on Hoth]]
Alliance crews referred to the weapon as the "150," and it was the single most powerful weapon in the Alliance's ground-based arsenal. However, despite the expense and usefulness of the weapon, it was considered a disposable weapon to use in desperate circumstances, and abandoned during the evacuation. On Hoth, the crew manning the ion cannon were soldiers from [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] who were willing and eager to [[Death/Legends|die]] at their posts to aid the Rebellion and hurt the Empire.<ref name="RASB">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref> Targeting data for the v-150 on Hoth was supplemented by Echo Base's electrotelescopes and long-range sensors.<ref name="EGWT" /> Its power generator was remotely connected to the base's main reactors, which were scavenged from a [[Praetor-class Star Battlecruiser/Legends|''Praetor''-class Star Battlecruiser]]. While v-150s were usually powered by reactors located forty meters below ground, the Echo Base generator was buried a full kilometer below the icy surface.<ref name="SWCL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref>

Before its abandonment, the cannon provided valuable cover fire for the escaping transports of Echo Base as they attempted to run the blockading line of [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron's]] [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers]] orbiting Hoth.<ref name="ESB" /> From the base's command center, head controller [[Toryn Farr/Legends|Toryn Farr]]<ref name="TF">{{CCG|set=Hoth Limited|cardname=Toryn Farr}}</ref> directed the ion cannon to fire upon the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Rebel Dream|''Tyrant'']], disabling it as the [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transport]] [[Quantum Storm/Legends|''Quantum Storm'']], the first transport to evacuate Hoth, slipped past the Imperial [[Warship/Legends|warship]] and entered [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]. The Alderaanian crew stayed at the posts until the end of the battle, then set the v-150 to explode to cover the last transports.<ref name="EGWT" />

However, the cannon itself was structurally intact and operational when [[Jaden Korr]] arrived in [[14 ABY/Legends|14 ABY]] searching for the [[Disciples of Ragnos]].<ref name="JA">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref> Two v-150 cannons were also present during Kyle Katarn's mission to [[Artus Prime]].<ref name="JO">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast]]''</ref>

The [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] used v-150s to defend poor but strategically important worlds. They proved almost useless against the [[Yuuzhan Vong]]'s [[Yuuzhan_Vong#Technology|biotechnology]].<ref name="NEGWT" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:MCQ-ioncannon.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Concept art of the v-150 by [[Ralph McQuarrie]]]]
The v-150 Planet Defender first appeared with the release of [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] and its tie-ins. The ion cannon at Echo Base subsequently appeared in many sources. One source states that the ion cannon was destroyed to cover the Rebels' escape, although two other sources contradict that. In ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'', a [[2001]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]], the player is assigned to destroy the ion cannon and must do so before proceeding to the next objective. In ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]'', a [[2003]] video game, the ion cannon at Hoth is intact. This article incorporates information from all three sources.

The ion cannon appears in the background of the Hoth map skirmish mission in the video game ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''. It fires throughout the match.
